t: Palenque was a Maya city-state whose known dynasty began with Kʼuk Balam in 431, and which was sacked by Calakmul and its client states in 599 and 611 before it recovered.
Kʼinich Janaabʼ Pakal ruled from 615 to 683 and, with his sons, built most of the palaces and temples that stand today; the city was sacked again by Toniná in 711.

Elite building at the ceremonial centre ended some time after 800, farmers stayed for a few generations, and the forest then grew over the site, which was visited, drawn and excavated by outsiders from 1773 onwards.
dyk: Pakal's tomb was entered in 1952 by Alberto Ruz Lhuillier, the first person to look on it in over a thousand years, after four years of work at the Temple of the Inscriptions; a jade mosaic mask lay over the king's face.
ev: The date from which the ruins of Palenque are dated
Kʼuk Balam begins to rule as the first known king of the city-state
Troops from Calakmul invade and sack Palenque
Kʼinich Janaabʼ Pakal begins his reign of nearly seventy years
Pakal dies and his son Kʼinich Kan Bʼalam becomes king
Toniná sacks Palenque and takes Kʼinich Kʼan Joy Chitam II prisoner
Elite building at the ceremonial centre comes to an end
Alberto Ruz Lhuillier opens the passage to Pakal's tomb

f.founded: The ruins date from about 226 BCE; the first king of the city-state known by name, Kʼuk Balam, began to rule in 431, and he is supposed to have founded the dynasty.
f.where: Near the Usumacinta River in the Mexican state of Chiapas, about 130 km south of Ciudad del Carmen and 150 metres above sea level, beside the modern town of Palenque.
f.known: The reign of Kʼinich Janaabʼ Pakal (615 to 683); his tomb in the Temple of the Inscriptions; the Palace; the Temples of the Cross group; hieroglyphic inscriptions; the sacks of 599, 611 and 711; its aqueducts
f.today: Palenque is an excavated and restored archaeological site in Chiapas, protected since 1981 as Palenque National Park.
